title: Inguinal hernia surgery
what: The surgeon pushes the bulge back into place and strengthens the belly wall, usually with a special mesh. This is done through a cut in the groin or through small keyhole cuts.
why: For an inguinal hernia: a bulge in the groin that bothers you, hurts, or grows.
duration: surgery usually takes 30 to 90 minutes. You often go home the same day or the next
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. The doctor decides what to stop and when
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes
If you have had hernia surgery before
If you have had problems with anesthesia

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, and sometimes a checkup with a general doctor. Your clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Anesthesia
prepare.text: The surgery is done under general anesthesia, a spinal injection, or local anesthesia. The doctors decide what suits you.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food from the evening before, and no drinks for a few hours before. Your clinic will tell you the exact times.

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Take a shower. Shaving the groin beforehand is usually not needed. Check with your clinic.

steps: On the day of surgery, you change your clothes and a drip line is put into a vein
The surgeon puts the hernia back in place through a cut or keyhole cuts
The wall is strengthened with mesh, and the cut is stitched
After surgery, you rest in your room
feel: Pain and a pulling feeling in the groin. You will get pain medicine
A small bruise or swelling in the groin. It goes away on its own
For the first few days, getting up and coughing feel awkward
after: You can usually walk on the day of surgery
Usually no heavy lifting for 2 to 4 weeks. Your surgeon will tell you exactly
When you cough, hold your hand over the wound
Stitches are removed or dissolve on their own. Your surgeon will tell you which
red_flags: Before surgery: the hernia will not go back in, has become hard and painful, or you are vomiting. Call emergency services
After surgery: a fever above 38 degrees, redness, or pus at the wound
Severe swelling in the groin, or trouble peeing

faq.q: Can an inguinal hernia be treated without surgery?
faq.a: No. A support belt only holds it in. It does not get rid of the hernia. Only surgery can do that.

faq.q: Why is an inguinal hernia dangerous?
faq.a: It can get trapped. This is an emergency. If the hernia will not go back in and it hurts, call emergency services.

reminders.text: Surgery tomorrow. Pack your documents, test results, and list of medicines. Eat and drink only until the time your clinic gave you.
